Careers and Guidance
Wanting to find out more about Work Experience? Look here!
Our Careers team provide high-quality careers education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) to motivate and inspire our students. We aim to equip them with the skills, knowledge and information needed to achieve their full potential at school, work, and ultimately throughout their career.
The Careers Programme is structured, impartial, and embedded across the whole school. We adhere to statutory guidance on careers education, including ‘Careers guidance and access for education and training providers’ and work closely with the Careers and Enterprise Company to ensure compliance with relevant legislation. Click here for our: Provider Access Statement
We also use the Gatsby Charitable Foundation’s Benchmarks to develop and improve our careers provision. Find out more here: Good Career Guidance Report. The Gatsby Benchmarks ensure we are providing an outstanding programme of support for our students that is regularly reviewed to national standards.
Throughout our careers programme we collaborate with employers and post-16/18 learning providers including local colleges, sixth forms, universities and apprenticeship training providers. An Independent Careers Advisor provides 1:1 Career Interviews at key transitions, ensuring every student is receives bespoke support before they leave school. We also work with other organisations that aim to support young people in their transition from school into further learning or the workplace, including the Local Authority and National Citizen Service
Where possible, providers are invited into school to work with students through collapsed timetable days, events, assemblies, tutor sessions and targeted group work.
If you would like to learn more about our careers programme or about how you can get involved, please email: clockie@bohuntworthing.co.uk
Careers and Guidance
Careers Lead – Charley Lockie clockie@bohuntworthing.com
Measuring Success
Reviewing impact is a key part of what we do. Our careers provision is organic – it grows and changes with each cohort to ensure we are meeting the needs of students and providing relevant activities to help them shape their futures.
We work closely with the Local Authority in providing destinations data (also reported to our governors) and to provide intervention for students at risk of becoming NEET (not in education, employment, or training).
We regularly evaluate all of our workshops and events asking both students and providers to share their views in order to gauge impact and improve provision. Student progress is further reviewed using the Unifrog and Skills Builder toolkits, as well as the Future Skills Questionnaire to examine provision and impact across their time at Bohunt. This data, along with feedback from parents and carers, feeds into our annual action plans.
We formally assess our progress towards each of the 8 Gatsby Benchmarks each term using the Compass evaluation tool as part of our partnership working with the Careers and Enterprise Company.
Our next review will be November 2025
Careers Provision Overview
Aim: SKILLS – Understanding self: what am I good at?
“I really enjoyed the eco-gardens workshop – the people from Ricardo were interesting and I heard about jobs I didn’t know about”
Aim: PERSONALITY – Knowing strengths: what do I want?
“The assembly on languages has made me consider taking Mandarin at GCSE”
Aim: DEFINING – Linking careers and pathways: where could I go?
“Mentoring sessions helped me realise what I am actually good at. I feel much more confident.”
Aim: REFINING – Honing choices: how do I get there?
“The workshops were great! I really enjoyed ‘Women in Construction’ and would now consider a career in Town Planning. More please!”
Aim: DESTINATIONS – Beyond Bohunt & College Applications: Where am I going next?
“The Futures Fair has helped me work out where to go next. It was good to talk to different people. It doesn’t feel quite as intimidating now”

Careers in the Curriculum
Teaching staff and departments are aware of their important role in careers. Careers content is embedded into lessons and staff are actively working towards improving the ‘careers in the curriculum’ content for their subject. Increasingly, school trips aim to include Labour Market Information and provide opportunities to engage with employers in the workplace, with an aim to inspire students about potential career pathways.
Resources to support provision for teachers:

All staff also have access to Unifrog so that they can share LMI with students using the Careers Library tool.
We also encourage all staff to consider careers learning opportunities when running trips and events – such as requesting speakers to share their career journeys and provide work taster experiences.
Useful websites for students, parents and carers
All students are provided with a Unifrog account. This platform allows them to evaluate their skills, record their experience (CV), and research prospective colleges, apprenticeships, courses, and careers. Parents can also be allocated a log-in on request.

Gatsby Benchmarks
1. A stable careers programme
Every school and college should have an embedded programme of career education and guidance that is known and understood by pupils, parents, teachers and employers.
Every school should have a stable, structured careers programme that has the explicit backing of the senior management team, and has an identified and appropriately trained person responsible for it.The careers programme should be published on the school’s website in a way that enables pupils, parents, teachers and employers to access and understand it.The programme should be regularly evaluated with feedback from pupils, parents, teachers and employers as part of the evaluation process.
2. Learning from career and labour market information
Every pupil, and their parents, should have access to good quality information about future study options and labour market opportunities. They will need the support of an informed adviser to make the best use of available information.
By the age of 14, all pupils should have accessed and used information about career paths and the labour market to inform their own decisions on study options.Parents should be encouraged to access and use information about labour markets and future study options to inform their support to their children.
3. Addressing the needs of each individual
Pupils have different career guidance needs at different stages. Opportunities for advice and support need to be tailored to the needs of each pupil. A school’s careers programme should embed equality and diversity considerations throughout.
A school’s careers programme should actively seek to challenge stereotypical thinking and raise aspirations.Schools should keep systematic records of the individual advice given to each pupil, and subsequent agreed decisions.All pupils should have access to these records to support their career development.Schools should collect and maintain accurate data for each pupil on their education, training or employment destinations for at least three years after they leave the school.
4. Linking curriculum learning to careers
All teachers should link curriculum learning with careers. For example, STEM subject teachers should highlight the relevance of STEM subjects for a wide range of career pathways.
By the age of 14, every pupil should have had the opportunity to learn how the different STEM subjects help people to gain entry to, and be more effective workers within, a wide range of careers.
5. Encounters with employers and employees
Every pupil should have multiple opportunities to learn from employers about work, employment and the skills that are valued in the workplace. This can be through a range of enrichment opportunities including visiting speakers, mentoring and enterprise schemes.
Every year, from the age of 11, pupils should participate in at least one meaningful encounter* with an employer.* A ‘meaningful encounter’ is one in which the student has an opportunity to learn about what work is like or what it takes to be successful in the workplace.
6. Experience of workplaces
Every pupil should have first-hand experiences of the workplace through work visits, work shadowing and/or work experience to help their exploration of career opportunities, and expand their networks.
By the age of 16, every pupil should have had at least one experience of a workplace, additional to any part-time jobs they may have.By the age of 18, every pupil should have had one further such experience, additional to any part-time jobs they may have.
7. Encounters with further and higher education
All pupils should understand the full range of learning opportunities that are available to them. This includes both academic and vocational routes and learning in schools, colleges, universities and in the workplace.
By the age of 16, every pupil should have had a meaningful encounter* with providers of the full range of learning opportunities, including sixth forms, colleges, universities and apprenticeship providers. This should include the opportunity to meet both staff and pupils.By the age of 18, all pupils who are considering applying for university should have had at least two visits to universities to meet staff and pupils.* A ‘meaningful encounter’ is one in which the student has an opportunity to explore what it is like to learn in that environment.
8. Personal guidance
Every pupil should have opportunities for guidance interviews with a Careers Adviser, who could be internal (a member of school staff) or external, provided they are trained to an appropriate level. These should be available whenever significant study or career choices are being made. They should be expected for all pupils but should be timed to meet their individual needs.
Every pupil should have at least one such interview by the age of 16, and the opportunity for a further interview by the age of 18.

Gatsby Benchmarks

Provider Access Policy
This statement sets out our arrangements for managing the access of providers to students for the purpose of providing them with information about their education and/or work based training. This policy complies with the School’s statutory duties under sections 42A, 42B, 45 and 45A of the Education Act 1997, as amended by the Skills and Post-16 Education Act 2022, alongside the 2022 ‘Career Guidance and Access for Education and Training providers’ statutory guidance for schools.
Schools must ensure that there is an opportunity for a range of education and training providers to access students during the relevant phase of their education for the purpose of informing them about approved technical education qualifications or apprenticeships.
Pupil entitlement
Schools must provide the following number of encounters with providers of technical education or apprenticeships following the criteria specified in section 14 of the Skills and Post-16 Education Act 2022:
● ‘First Key Phase’ (Years 7-9): two encounters with two different providers
● ‘Second Key Phase’ (Years 10-11): two encounters with two different providers
All students in Years 7 to 11 are entitled to find out about, and understand how to make applications for the full range of education and training options available to them, (including technical and apprenticeship qualifications) as part of the School careers programme. This includes hearing from a range of education and training providers about the opportunities they offer, for example through school events, assemblies, school activities, and taster events.
Management of provider access requests
Any provider wishing to request access to the School for the purposes of providing students with information about education and training opportunities should contact the School’s designated Careers lead, Charley Lockie at clockie@bohuntworthing.com
Opportunities for access
Providers are welcome to speak with our designated careers lead to identify the most suitable opportunity for them. All requests to access students for the purposes of providing information and guidance related to education and training opportunities will be considered on an individual basis, including factors such as whether a suitable opportunity and appropriate facilities are available
Refer to the main careers page for details of internal and external provision
Please speak to our Careers Leader, Charley Lockie, to identify the most suitable opportunity for you.
Premises and facilities
The School will make the main hall, classrooms, or meeting rooms available for discussions between the provider and students as appropriate to the activity. Providers are welcome to leave a copy of their prospectus or other relevant course literature for display in our careers library, or share an electronic version to be distributed via careers google classroom.

Report an Absence
There is a clear correlation between excellent attendance and exceptional achievement. We work closely with parents and children to ensure students are meeting a minimum of 96% attendance.
Reporting an absence
To report your child absent from school, please use the StudyBugs app. All parents and carers should have downloaded the app if at all possible, at the start of term. You can download the app here: studybugs.com/about/parents
Alternatively, you can go to http://studybugs and report your child’s absence via this website.
In line with government guidance, we do not ask for evidence that your child is unwell as standard. We are likely to ask for evidence if your child has an extended period of time. If you are concerned your child is likely to be unwell for an extended period we would advise for you to gather evidence at your convenience.
This evidence could be evidence of a medical appointment, a prescription or a review with a pharmacist. Alternatively, if your child is following advice to not visit a doctor then a picture of a thermometer showing a high temperature would be adequate (as an example).
Should you have any issues downloading the app, logging in or adding your child please get in touch with Studybugs directly by emailing support@studybugs.com.
In the rare case that you are unable to use Studybugs to report an absence, you may ring the school on (01903) 601361 and leave a message.
Medical appointments
Wherever possible, medical/dental appointments should be arranged outside school hours. Where this is not possible a request for absence form must be submitted, or in the event of an emergency appointment being obtained, evidence must be provided. Failure to provide either of those may result in the absence being unauthorised.
Holidays
Headteachers have been directed by the Government not to authorise any absence from school unless there is an ‘exceptional’ circumstance.. In these circumstances, parents/carers must apply to the Headteacher using the Request for Leave of Absence Form which can be collected from reception. Any holiday taken, which has been applied for and declined, and which involved 10 or more sessions (5 school days of absence) will result in a referral for a Fixed Penalty Notice (FPN) being issued and subsequent fine.
